title: Solvent-controlled intramolecular [2 + 2] photocycloadditions of α-substituted enones
authors: Ng, Stephanie M.; Bader, Scott J.; Snapper, Marc L.
citation: Journal of the American Chemical Society (2006), 128(22), 7315-7319
reference: Solvent-controlled intramolecular [2 + 2] photocycloadditions of α-substituted enones | Ng, Stephanie M.; Bader, Scott J.; Snapper, Marc L. | Journal of the American Chemical Society (2006), 128(22), 7315-7319
experimental_procedure: To a flame-dried Schlenk flask purged with N2 was added ketone 31 (38.5 mg, 0.165 mmol) in toluene (0.825 mL). (S)-Methyl-3,3-diphenyl-1H,3H-pyrrolo[1,2-c][1,3,2]-oxazaborole (0.082 mmol, 1M in toluene) was added dropwise and the flask was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. A solution of BH3.THF (0.165 mmol, 1 M THF) was added dropwise and stirred for 15 min at 0 °C and then quenched with MeOH (1 mL). The reaction mixture was stirred for 15 min, then warmed to room temperature and allowed to stir for another 15 min before opening the flask to air. Aqueous HCl (2 mL, 1 M) was added and the reaction mixture was stirred for 1 h. The reaction mixture was then diluted with Et2O (10 mL) and washed with brine (5 mL). The combined organic layers were dried with MgSO4 and concentrated in vacuo. The product was purified on silica gel (pentane:Et2O 1:1) to give enone 27 (18.9 mg, 60%) as a pale yellow oil. 2-((R)-2-((R)-cyclopent-2-enyl)-1-hydroxyethyl)cyclopent-2-enone (27): Rf 0.28 (pentane:Et2O 2:3);. 1H-NMR (CDCl3, 400 MHz) δ 7.44 (td, 1H, J = 2.4, 0.8 Hz), 5.73 (m, 1H), 5.67 (m, 1H), 4.52 (m, 1H), 2.85 (m, 2H), 2.61 (m, 2H), 2.44 (m, 2H), 2.31 (m, 1H), 2.10 (dtd, 1H, J = 12.8, 8.0, 4.4 Hz), 1.82 (m, 1H), 1.56 (ddd, 1H, J = 13.2, 9.2, 4.0 Hz), 1.45 (m, 1H). 13C-NMR (CDCl3, 125 MHz) δ 210.2, 157.8, 148.3, 135.2, 130.8, 67.0, 42.3, 42.2, 35.4, 35.0, 29.9, 26.8. experimental_procedure: Transformation of C-B bond to hydroxy group; (1R*,2R*)-2-[(1S*,2S*)-1,4-Dimethyl-2-hydroxypentyl]-1-cycloheptanol (21). A solution of the ketone 20 (0.180 g, 0.54 mmol, 90% ds) in methanol was slowly added to 5% palladium on carbon (0.5 g) under nitrogen atmosphere. The reaction vessel was put in an autoclave and then pressurized with hydrogen (20 atm). After 2 h, hydrogen was released. The reaction mixture was filtered with a pad of Florisil® by using Et2O as an eluent. After removal of methanol in vacuo, BH3·THF (1.0 M in THF, 1.6 mL, 1.6 mmol) was added to the crude product at -78°C. The reaction mixture was gradually warmed to 0°C and stirred for 3 h at that temperature. THF and unreacted BH 3 were removed in vacuo. Methanol (5.0 mL) and 30% aqueous H2O2 (1.0 mL) were added in tern at 0 °C. The reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature for 1 h. Saturated aqueous Na2S2O3 (5.0 mL) was slowly added at 0°C. Methanol was removed in vacuo, and then the aqueous layer was extracted with Et2O five times. The combined organic layers were washed with brine, dried over anhydrous Na2SO4, and filtrated. The solvents were removed in vacuo. The resulting crude product was purified with column chromatography on silica gel (30, 50% Et2O in hexane) to give the title compound (0.099 g, 81% yield, 85% ds determined by 1H NMR analysis) as a colorless liquid. authors: Bosiak, Mariusz J.; Pakulski, Marcin M.
reference: Asymmetric reduction of α-keto aldoxime O-ethers | Bosiak, Mariusz J.; Pakulski, Marcin M. | Synthesis (2011), (2), 316-324
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Reduction of α-Keto Aldoxime O-Ethers with Borane/Oxazaborolidine; General Procedure : To a solution of the appropriate amino alcohol (2 mmol) in THF (10 mL) was added 10 M BMS (borane-methyl sulfide complex) (0.2 mL, 2 mmol) and the mixture was stirred at r.t. for 1 h. THF (5 mL) and the rest of BMS (0.8 mL, 8 mmol) were added and the mixture was stirred for another 10 min. The mixture was cooled to 0 °C and α-keto aldoxime ether (2 mmol) in THF (15 mL) was added in 2.5 h using a syringe pump. The mixture was stirred at 0 °C for 10 min, at r.t. for 30 min, and refluxed for 18 h. After cooling to r.t., aq 3 M HCl (12 mL) was added slowly and the mixture was allowed to stir for 5 h. THF was removed on a rotary evaporator; then EtOAc (30 mL) and NaCl (5 g) were added to the residue, and the mixture was basified with aq 10% NaOH to pH 12 and stirred for 5 min. The organic layer was separated and the residue was extracted with EtOAc (5 x 15 mL). The combined organic extracts were dried (MgSO4). The solvent was removed and the product was isolated by flash chromatography on silica gel (CH2Cl2-MeOH, 90:10). The product was derivatized with trifluoroacetic anhydride in the presence of Et3N and analyzed by GC on a chiral β-Dex 325 capillary column (30 m x 0.25 mm). Commercially available chiral 2-amino-1-phenylethanols were also derivatized with trifluoroacetic anhydride and analyzed by GC as comparative samples. (R)-2-Amino-1-(4-methoxyphenyl)ethanol (30), yield 74%, 50% ee. mp 70-72 °C (Lit. mp 73-75 °C). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Asymmetric Reduction of Acetophenone with Catalyst 2; Typical Procedure. A 100 mL, flame-dried, two-necked, round-bottomed flask equipped with a magnetic stirrer bar was charged with catalyst 2 (0.66 mmol) and anhyd THF (4 mL). PhCOMe (2 mmol, 0.22 mL) was then added under argon from a syringe. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Isolation of Alcohols. The following procedure is for larger scale reactions. In the assembly previously described was placed 20 mL of 1.0 M BH3-THF solution (20 mmol). Into the solution was injected 7.4 g of 2-methylcyclohexanone (66 mmol). The reaction was brought to gentle reflux, and the reaction mixture was stirred for 5 d. The mixture was then hydrolyzed with 20 mL of 3 N HCl and saturated with NaCl. The separated organic layer was dried over anhydrous K2CO3. All the volatile materials were evaporated under reduced pressure and fractional distillation gave 5.5 g (81% yield) of essentially pure 2-methylcyclohexanol, bp 165-167 °C (759 mm). GC examination revealed the presence of a trace amount of cis- and >99.5% trans-2-methylcyclohexanol. Yield 7%

authors: Cha, Jin Soon; Moon, Suk Joung; Park, Jae Hyung
reference: A Solution of Borane in Tetrahydrofuran. A Stereoselective Reducing Agent for Reduction of Cyclic Ketones to Thermodynamically More Stable Alcohols | Cha, Jin Soon; Moon, Suk Joung; Park, Jae Hyung | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2001), 66(22), 7514-7515
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Isolation of Alcohols. The following procedure is for larger scale reactions. In the assembly previously described was placed 20 mL of 1.0 M BH3-THF solution (20 mmol). Into the solution was injected 7.4 g of 2-methylcyclohexanone (66 mmol). The reaction was brought to gentle reflux, and the reaction mixture was stirred for 5 d. The mixture was then hydrolyzed with 20 mL of 3 N HCl and saturated with NaCl. The separated organic layer was dried over anhydrous K2CO3. All the volatile materials were evaporated under reduced pressure and fractional distillation gave 5.5 g (81% yield) of essentially pure 2-methylcyclohexanol, bp 165-167 °C (759 mm). GC examination revealed the presence of a trace amount of cis- and >99.5% trans-2-methylcyclohexanol. Yield 82%

experimental_procedure: (2R)-7-Benzyloxy-3-[[2-(9-fluorenylmethoxycarbonylamino)-1-hydroxy]propyl]-1H-indole (27). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Isolation of Alcohols. The following procedure is for larger scale reactions. In the assembly previously described was placed 20 mL of 1.0 M BH3-THF solution (20 mmol). Into the solution was injected 7.4 g of 2-methylcyclohexanone (66 mmol). The reaction was brought to gentle reflux, and the reaction mixture was stirred for 5 d. The mixture was then hydrolyzed with 20 mL of 3 N HCl and saturated with NaCl. The separated organic layer was dried over anhydrous K2CO3. All the volatile materials were evaporated under reduced pressure and fractional distillation gave 5.5 g (81% yield) of essentially pure 2-methylcyclohexanol, bp 165-167 °C (759 mm). GC examination revealed the presence of a trace amount of cis- and >99.5% trans-2-methylcyclohexanol. 2-methylcyclohexanol, Yield 100% bp 165-167 °C (759 mm).
notes: stereoselective, alternative reaction conditions gave lower yield

experimental_procedure: The precatalyst (54.50 mg, 0.05 mmol) was dissolved, in 1 mL of 1M BH3-THF (1 mmol, nonstabilized) in THF (2 equiv BH3).under argon atmosphere at room temperature and stirred for one hour. Then a solution of ketone (0.5 mmol) in 1 mL of dry THF was added slowly over a period of one hour. The reaction mixture was stirred for additional 30 minutes to complete. Then it was cooled to 0 °C and quenched with 0.5 mL of MeOH. Addition of 2.5 mL of water to the reaction mixture induced the instant precipitation of precatalyst . This heterogeneous mixture was loaded on and filtered through fluorous silica gel (FluoroFlashTM) followed by acetonitrile-water 1:1(4X2.5 mL) washing to elute all nonfluorous products. Then the combined filtrates were concentrated in vacuo to remove organic solvents and the chiral secunder alcohol was extracted with chloroform (3X5 mL). The combined organic phases was dried over Na2SO4and evaporated in vacuo to give product. Yield. 99%. 1H-NMR (200 MHz, CDCl3) 7.40-7.25 (m, 5H, ArH), 4.88 (q, J= 6.3 Hz, 1H, CHOH), 2.10 (br s, 1H, OH), 1.49 (d, J = 6.3 Hz, 3H, CH3CH); 13C-NMR (50MHz, CD3Cl) 145.9 (C), 128.6 (CH), 127.6 (CH), 125.5 (CH), 70.5 (CH), 25.2 (CH3).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Potassium 4-Hydroxyethylphenyltrifluoroborate (3a). 4- Acetylphenylboronic acid (1.00 g, 6.10 mmol) was dissolved in anhyd EtOH (5.0 mL) and cooled 0 °C with an ice/water bath. NaBH4 (579 mg, 15.2 mmol) was added all at once as a solid. After stirring for 16 h, additional EtOH (5.0 mL) was added and the mixture was stirred for 4 h. The soln was cooled to 0 °C and treated with 1N HCl (30 mL, 30 mmol). The mixture was then extracted with EtOAc (3 X 15 mL), dried (Na2SO4), and concentrated. The crude boronic acid was then dissolved in MeOH (10 mL) and cooled to 0 °C. Satd aq KHF2 (6.8 mL, 31 mmol) was added dropwise via syringe. The mixture was stirred at 0 °C for 2 h, concentrated, and placed under high-vacuum (0.001 Torr) for 3 h. The dried solids were triturated with hot acetone (3 X 20 mL) and filtered to remove inorganicsalts. The resulting filtrate was concentrated and Et2O was added to precipitate a white solid (1.15 g, 83%): Potassium 3-(1-Hydroxyethyl)phenyltrifluoroborate (3b). experimental_procedure: General Procedure for Amine-Borane Transfer Hydrogenation of Imines and Ketones: All reactions were performed on a 0.3 mmol scale. To an oven-dried 2 mL septumcapped vial was added pyrrolidine-borane (3.0 equiv.) and a stir bar. This was placed under an Ar atmosphere by purging with an Ar-filled balloon. In a separate vial purged with Ar equipped with a stir bar, was placed 3 (0.015 equiv.) and dry KOtBu (0.03 equiv.). To this was added 0.5 mL of dry THF, and this solution was stirred for 5 minutes (turns purple). This solution was subsequently added via a syringe to the vial containing the amine-borane. Then, the imine or ketone (1.0 equiv.) was dissolved in 1 mL of dry THF, and this solution was added dropwise via a syringe to the septum-capped vial. Concentration of the substrate was 0.2 M. This orange solution was stirred for 3 hours at RT (imines) or 5.5 hours at RT (ketones). The reaction was subsequently concentrated in vacuo, and the crude mixture was subjected to column chromtography using 5% MeOH in DCM for the imine substrates or 5 to 10% EtOAc in Hexanes for the ketone substrates, providing the pure amine or alcohol products. Isolated Yield : 97%. This compound is commercially available. CAS # 98-85-1. 1H NMR (400MHz, CDCl3, 293K, TMS): 7.34 (4 H, m), 7.27 (1 H, m), 4.82 (1 H, q, J=6.8Hz), 2.74 (1 H, br s), 1.46 (3 H, d, J=6.8Hz).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Asymmetric Reduction of Acetophenone with Catalyst 2; Typical Procedure. A 100 mL, flame-dried, two-necked, round-bottomed flask equipped with a magnetic stirrer bar was charged with catalyst 2 (0.66 mmol) and anhyd THF (4 mL). PhCOMe (2 mmol, 0.22 mL) was then added under argon from a syringe. Subsequently, BH3•THF (2.4 mmol, 1.2 equiv) was added dropwise with the aid of a syringe pump at a rate of 1 mL/h, and the solution was then stirred at r.t. under argon for 18 h. When the reaction was complete, the mixture was hydrolyzed by addition of MeOH (5 mL) and 1 M aq HCl (5 mL). Workup as described in ref. 14 gave enantiomerically enriched 1-phenylethanol as a colorless oil; yield: 0.19 g (78%). (1S)-1-(2-Anthryl)ethanol(4e) 18. ee 10% (catalyst B). HPLC: Lux Cellulose-1, hexane-i-PrOH (90:10); flow rate: 1.0 mL/min, λ = 254 nm; tR (S) = 12.7 min, tR (R) = 21.3 min.

experimental_procedure: Typical Experimental Procedure for the Racemic Reduction of Acetophenone. In an oven-dried round-bottom flask, the stabilized borane solution (Aldrich 176192, 650412, or 630390, ca. 1 M in THF, 13.3 mmol) was diluted with 2 volumes of anhydrous THF. The diluted solution was cooled to 0 °C. Acetophenone (10 mmol) was added over 5 min. The reaction mixture was stirred with a magnetic stirrer at room temperature for 2 h. The reaction was quenched by addition of H2O (10 mL). Ether (10 mL) was added. The mixture was washed with 3 M HCl (10 mL). The organic phase was washed with H2O (10 mL) and brine (10 mL), dried over magnesium sulfate, and filtered. The solvent was removed to record the crude yield and for GC quantification. The clear liquid was passed through a silica gel plug (2 cm × 4 cm i.d.) with ether (100 mL). After the solvent was removed, the yield of isolated product was obtained by GC and weighing. (iii) Reduction of acetophenone using BTHF stabilized with NIMBA: yield (98% by GC; isolated 1.15 g (95%)). GC was run on HP5890 and an RTx-50 column with retention time 3.998 min.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Reduction of α-Keto Aldoxime O-Ethers with Borane/Oxazaborolidine; General Procedure : To a solution of the appropriate amino alcohol (2 mmol) in THF (10 mL) was added 10 M BMS (borane-methyl sulfide complex) (0.2 mL, 2 mmol) and the mixture was stirred at r.t. for 1 h. THF (5 mL) and the rest of BMS (0.8 mL, 8 mmol) were added and the mixture was stirred for another 10 min. The mixture was cooled to 0 °C and α-keto aldoxime ether (2 mmol) in THF (15 mL) was added in 2.5 h using a syringe pump. The mixture was stirred at 0 °C for 10 min, at r.t. for 30 min, and refluxed for 18 h. After cooling to r.t., aq 3 M HCl (12 mL) was added slowly and the mixture was allowed to stir for 5 h. THF was removed on a rotary evaporator; then EtOAc (30 mL) and NaCl (5 g) were added to the residue, and the mixture was basified with aq 10% NaOH to pH 12 and stirred for 5 min. The organic layer was separated and the residue was extracted with EtOAc (5 x 15 mL). The combined organic extracts were dried (MgSO4). The solvent was removed and the product was isolated by flash chromatography on silica gel (CH2Cl2-MeOH, 90:10). The product was derivatized with trifluoroacetic anhydride in the presence of Et3N and analyzed by GC on a chiral β-Dex 325 capillary column (30 m x 0.25 mm). Commercially available chiral 2-amino-1-phenylethanols were also derivatized with trifluoroacetic anhydride and analyzed by GC as comparative samples. Yield 81%. mp 59-62 °C (Lit. mp 60-62 °C). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Reduction of α-Keto Aldoxime O-Ethers with Borane/Oxazaborolidine; General Procedure : To a solution of the appropriate amino alcohol (2 mmol) in THF (10 mL) was added 10 M BMS (borane-methyl sulfide complex) (0.2 mL, 2 mmol) and the mixture was stirred at r.t. for 1 h. THF (5 mL) and the rest of BMS (0.8 mL, 8 mmol) were added and the mixture was stirred for another 10 min. The mixture was cooled to 0 °C and α-keto aldoxime ether (2 mmol) in THF (15 mL) was added in 2.5 h using a syringe pump. The mixture was stirred at 0 °C for 10 min, at r.t. for 30 min, and refluxed for 18 h. After cooling to r.t., aq 3 M HCl (12 mL) was added slowly and the mixture was allowed to stir for 5 h. THF was removed on a rotary evaporator; then EtOAc (30 mL) and NaCl (5 g) were added to the residue, and the mixture was basified with aq 10% NaOH to pH 12 and stirred for 5 min. The organic layer was separated and the residue was extracted with EtOAc (5 x 15 mL). The combined organic extracts were dried (MgSO4). The solvent was removed and the product was isolated by flash chromatography on silica gel (CH2Cl2-MeOH, 90:10). The product was derivatized with trifluoroacetic anhydride in the presence of Et3N and analyzed by GC on a chiral β-Dex 325 capillary column (30 m x 0.25 mm). Commercially available chiral 2-amino-1-phenylethanols were also derivatized with trifluoroacetic anhydride and analyzed by GC as comparative samples. citation: Journal of the American Chemical Society (2008), 130(43), 14034-14035
reference: Ruthenium-Catalyzed Dehydrogenation of Ammonia Boranes | Blaquiere, Nicole; Diallo-Garcia, Sarah; Gorelsky, Serge I.; Black, Daniel A.; Fagnou, Keith | Journal of the American Chemical Society (2008), 130(43), 14034-14035
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for Amine-Borane Transfer Hydrogenation of Imines and Ketones: All reactions were performed on a 0.3 mmol scale. To an oven-dried 2 mL septumcapped vial was added pyrrolidine-borane (3.0 equiv.) and a stir bar. This was placed under an Ar atmosphere by purging with an Ar-filled balloon. In a separate vial purged with Ar equipped with a stir bar, was placed 3 (0.015 equiv.) and dry KOtBu (0.03 equiv.). To this was added 0.5 mL of dry THF, and this solution was stirred for 5 minutes (turns purple). This solution was subsequently added via a syringe to the vial containing the amine-borane. Then, the imine or ketone (1.0 equiv.) was dissolved in 1 mL of dry THF, and this solution was added dropwise via a syringe to the septum-capped vial. Concentration of the substrate was 0.2 M. This orange solution was stirred for 3 hours at RT (imines) or 5.5 hours at RT (ketones). The reaction was subsequently concentrated in vacuo, and the crude mixture was subjected to column chromtography using 5% MeOH in DCM for the imine substrates or 5 to 10% EtOAc in Hexanes for the ketone substrates, providing the pure amine or alcohol products. Isolated Yield : 97%. This compound is commercially available. CAS # 3391-10-4. 1H NMR (400MHz, CDCl3, 293K, TMS): 7.24 (4 H, m), 4.77 (1 H, q, J=6.4Hz), 2.72 (1 H, br s), 1.40 (3 H, d, J=6.4Hz).
